title: arXiv Trending AI — Daily — 2026-10-23
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred notable-recent-paper ordering, not a popularity ranking. Citation evidence is limited for very recent papers, and Semantic Scholar requests were rate-limited, so no citation totals or citation velocity were used.

sections.title: Tool-Calling LLM Agents Under Realistic MCP Faults: Scale Does Not Purchase Fault Tolerance
sections.abstract: The authors introduce MCP-Injector, a protocol-aware fault-injection middleware calibrated from public MCP incidents, and report substantial task-quality degradation under injected faults across a 1,350-cell study.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors contribute a reproducible, stack-agnostic MCP fault injector and report that, for the two tested GPT-OSS backbones, greater model scale did not improve the share of fault-free performance retained under injected faults.
sections.unique_caveat: The scaling comparison covers only GPT-OSS 20B and 120B, three agent stacks, and 25 MCP-Bench tasks; the calibrated incident corpus reflects public repositories collected in September 2025.

sections.title: IGG: A Benchmark for Interactive GUI Grounding under Visibility Constraints
sections.abstract: IGG measures whether GUI agents can reveal hidden or unavailable targets through interaction before locating and clicking them, using 601 tasks across 16 controllable environments.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a benchmark that separates visibility recovery from static grounding and end-to-end navigation, and report that supervised fine-tuning followed by online GRPO improves visibility recovery across three VLM architectures.
sections.unique_caveat: The benchmark uses 16 controllable, mock GUI environments and a compact five-action interface, so performance on live applications and unconstrained GUI workflows remains unestablished.

sections.title: When Agents Fail: Model or Harness--Who's to Blame?
sections.abstract: The authors evaluate model–harness interactions using five measures across 111 settings and 52,168 trajectories, finding that rankings and valid completion vary by model, harness, and benchmark.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose Valid Completion Rate, Model–Harness Fit, Cross-Model Fit, Interaction Residuals, and Token Load to distinguish successful task execution from operational completion and pairing-specific behavior.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported comparisons cover the named harnesses, models, adapter, and six benchmark suite; the aggregate ranking should not be treated as universal across other agent frameworks or tasks.

sections.title: Accordion: Elastic-Depth Inference via Fixed-Prefix Layer Looping
sections.abstract: Accordion combines fixed-prefix layer looping with budget-specific execution paths to offer five inference budgets in one model, reporting depth-dependent gains across 37 tasks after 3.6T tokens of pretraining.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors claim fixed-prefix layer looping can provide elastic inference depth without separate models per budget, reporting a 3.01-point five-category macro-average gain as inference depth increases, with the middle budget obtaining most of the gain at fewer extra layer executions.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported results center on the Accordion-6B-A0.5B model and the paper’s 37-task suite; scaling the method to larger families and workloads is not demonstrated in the abstract.

sections.title: Beyond Post-Hoc Rewards: Privileged Reasoning Exploration for Multimodal Embeddings
sections.abstract: PILOT uses training-time relational evidence to explore retrieval-relevant reasoning traces and selectively transfers useful traces to an inference-compatible prior, reporting gains on MMEB-V2 at 2B and 7B parameters.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors model reasoning as a latent variable with separate input-only prior and relation-informed posterior modes, using an importance-weighted objective to transfer useful training-time exploration to inference.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported retrieval gains are measured on MMEB-V2; the abstract does not establish that the method transfers to other multimodal tasks or evaluation suites.

sections.title: OWLS: Open-world Language-conditioned Speed Fields for Zero-Shot Rover Navigation
sections.abstract: OWLS turns open-vocabulary VLM terrain scores into speed fields for minimum-time rover planning, and evaluates the approach on a physical rover, simulated planetary terrains, and real planetary imagery.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose a training-free planner that projects language-conditioned VLM traversability scores into a ground-plane speed field and combines terrain appearance with obstacle clearance.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported tests cover the described rover, simulation, and imagery settings; robustness across other platforms, sensors, and field conditions is not established by the abstract.

sections.title: LGMT: A Tool for Testing the Logical Reasoning Reliability of LLMs
sections.abstract: LGMT tests whether LLM entailment predictions remain consistent across logically equivalent reformulations, using 20 built-in metamorphic relations and a 3,091-group benchmark.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present a CLI/web tool that checks consistency across first-order-logic-equivalent cases, including custom relations verified with Z3, and report inconsistency rates between 20.84% and 29.44% for the tested models.
sections.unique_caveat: Metamorphic agreement tests consistency, not whether a prediction is logically correct; the reported rates apply to the selected relations, bundled cases, and six models.
